summary: Plumas NF lookout on Grizzly Ridge: construction began 1934, staffed until 1980, now a restoration-group rebuild under a 2021 MOU/MOA.

facts.design: Enclosed tower with C-3 cab and catwalk

visit.trail_note: 2005 register visit: good gravel road, 7 miles from pavement and 6 miles east of Quincy; last half mile rough, 2WD OK.

events.note: Construction on the enclosed tower began in 1934, per the register
Register gives 1936 as first staffed year; 1937 papers describe the summit as newly manned
New Forest Service station completed in early November 1937; the temporary lookout building was blown off the rock days later in a windstorm
Lookout put out a grass fire about 50 feet from the station, started by a stray match
Register says the lookout was in active service until 1980
Quincy/Greenville Ranger District sought public comment on restoring the lookout, no longer used
Register visit: roof failing, stairs missing, cab floor poor
MOU/MOA signed for the lookout's rehabilitation (the counterparty is not named in the source)
A formal group/subchapter was formed after the MOU/MOA and was awarded a large RAC grant (amount not stated)
The group built new steel access stairs and stairs to the cab and began rebuilding the lookout; project listed as ongoing

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says construction began in 1934. The November 1937 papers describe a temporary building used in 1937 and a permanent station completed that month, so the 1934 date is the start of construction and 1937 is when the current station was finished.

The register gives 1936 as the first staffed year. An August 1937 paper says the summit had recently been turned into a manned lookout, which points to 1937 as the first year the station was manned, though the sources do not state it outright.

notes_for_editor: Distance from Quincy is disputed: the register's 2005 visit says 6 miles east, a 1937 Plumas Independent item says about 12 miles east. Not resolved; the story reports both. The record's 'built 1934' is the register's construction-start date; the newspapers show the permanent station completed in November 1937. A human should decide whether the built field needs a correction. The register's 11' figure is not labelled (cab, tower or height), so no height_m is given. The record's event 2025 'restored' overstates the FFLA report, which lists the work as ongoing; it is recorded here as 'other'. The FFLA California list at firelookout.org/lookouts/us/ca/ agrees with the register: Encl. Tower, Standing, NHLR US 601, CA 72.Access level is not stated by any source read, and the last register visit is from 2005, so access and climbability are left out. Staffing 'unstaffed' rests on the 2005 register visit, which is old. The 1994 notice names the Quincy/Greenville Ranger District; the register now names the Mt. Hough Ranger District.
